comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C3, C47-C49. Both evaluations find the toolbox's core capabilities and Python implementation fully supported. OpenEval cites demonstrated applications and prior work; peer reviewers explicitly affirm utility as 'fundamental work' and 'great asset to the brain imaging community.'

Disagreement on evaluation type for claims C12, C14, C40-C41. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on Figure 1 results, noting comparative validation not shown but conceptually sound. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 requesting synthetic data validation to test whether method 'can keep up as data is made more challenging.'

Perfect agreement on claims C15-C18. Both evaluations find the network identification and task-related activations fully supported. OpenEval cites Figure 2 with appropriate statistics; peer reviewers note methods are 'well described' and see expected similarities across runs and tasks.

Perfect agreement on claims C19-C23. Both evaluations support the state-specific spectral properties and consistency findings. OpenEval references Figures 3-4 with citations; peer Reviewer 2 explicitly confirms 'similarities between states across multiple runs and across tasks and even methods.'

Disagreement on evaluation type for claims C24-C27, C67. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on Figure 4BI statistics and citation to Coquelet et al. 2020. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 requesting better explanation of why sensory-motor areas show differences and visual network lifetime decreases.

Perfect agreement on claims C28-C33. Both evaluations support DyNeMo's network identification and age-related differences. OpenEval notes stronger effect size with appropriate caveats; peer reviewers accept findings and confirm that questions about objective model comparison have been addressed in revision.

Agreement on claims C42-C44, C71-C72 (partial overlap with C45-C46, C73). Both evaluations support the methodological distinctions and complementary nature of HMM vs DyNeMo. OpenEval cites Figure 7 and Gohil et al. 2022; peer Reviewer 3 confirms questions about objective model comparison have been addressed.

Agreement on claims C45-C46 (partial overlap with R7). Both evaluations support DyNeMo's ability to capture overlapping spatial modes. OpenEval cites Gohil et al. 2022 for validation; peer reviewers accept the comparative framework without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C50-C52. Both evaluations support the limitations of sliding window approaches and advantages of generative models. OpenEval cites Liuzzi et al. 2019; peer Reviewer 3 affirms methods are 'principled, based on generative probabilistic models.'

Perfect agreement on claims C53-C58. Both evaluations support the HMM and DyNeMo methodological descriptions. OpenEval references extensive citations and Figure 7; peer Reviewer 3 states methods are 'well described and demonstrated within multiple peer reviewed articles.'

Perfect agreement on claims C59-C62. Both evaluations support the TDE methodology description. OpenEval references Figure 9C and mathematical relationships; peer Reviewer 3 notes 'few initial assumptions are necessary,' aligning with data-driven nature of TDE.

Agreement on claims C63-C66 (partial overlap with C88-C91). Both evaluations support the training procedure and reproducibility approach. OpenEval cites supplementary figures; peer Reviewer 2 initially requested clarification but confirms 'authors have addressed all concerns raised earlier.'

Agreement on claims C88-C91 (partial overlap with R12). Both evaluations support the variational inference characteristics and reproducibility criteria. OpenEval notes these are standard considerations; peer reviewers accept the reproducibility approach after revision.

Agreement on claims C75-C76 (partial overlap with C74). Both evaluations support validation through prior work citations. OpenEval notes validation not shown in manuscript but appropriately cited; peer Reviewer 2 acknowledges existing validation work while requesting additional synthetic validation for specific applications.

Agreement on claim C74 (partial overlap). Both evaluations support the static network analysis demonstration. OpenEval references Section 2.5 and Figure 6; peer reviewers accept the approach as part of broader validation framework.

Agreement on claims C69-C70. Both evaluations recognize these as speculative interpretations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are 'explicitly stated as speculative explanations' without direct validation; peer reviewers accept as reasonable possibilities that could be expanded.

Overlap on claim C67. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN within broader context of C67-C70, noting citation to Coquelet et al. 2020 but speculative mechanistic claims. Peer review also rates related claims as UNCERTAIN, requesting better explanation of age-related differences.

Overlap on claim C73. OpenEval supports C73 as reasonable criterion for model evaluation; peer reviewers accept the comparative framework, with Reviewer 3 confirming questions about objective model comparison have been addressed.

Perfect agreement on claims C78-C87. Both evaluations support the methodological details and implementation choices. OpenEval notes appropriate documentation with citations; peer Reviewer 3 states methods are 'principled' and 'well described.'

Perfect agreement on claims C4-C11. Both evaluations support the background neuroscience context as well-cited and established. OpenEval notes accurate representation of cited literature; peer reviewers do not challenge these motivating claims, focusing instead on novel contributions.
